statements.status_notes: Adapter pf-google-chrome-enterprise-device-trust-adapter-1.0.jar shades jackson-databind 2.14.3, which is above the vulnerable range. In addition, the vulnerable condition for CVE-2020-36518 requires enabling default typing or performing untyped deserialization of untrusted input. Our adapter’s code (incl. ObjectMapperUtil) does neither. Static analysis found no calls to enableDefaultTyping/activateDefaultTyping, and no untyped readValue(..., Object.class) usage. Deserialization targets typed DTOs only. Therefore the CVE’s preconditions are not met. The adapter centralizes JSON configuration in ObjectMapperUtil#getDefault(), which constructs an ObjectMapper and sets JsonInclude.Include.NON_NULL and FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES=false. It does not enable default typing nor any polymorphic/untyped deserialization features.
PingFederate deploys the pf-google-connector conditionally. The pf-google-connector ships with log4j, but the chainsaw dependency is unused at runtime.

False Positive. The PingFederate adapter does not parse input files from untrusted sources. In order to maintain a good security posture, PingFederate and the usercount.jar library has been scheduled for an upgrade TODO add jira.
